context.body: Ephesus and the road to Jerusalem · Acts 20:17–38
context.label: Ephesus and the road to Jerusalem

observations.body: Paul speaks farewell to the Ephesian elders. From Miletus he sent to Ephesus and called to himself the elders of the assembly. sorrowing most of all because of the word which he had spoken, that they should see his face no more. Then they accompanied him to the ship.
observations.label: Paul speaks farewell to the Ephesian elders

observations.body: The passage presents Paul speaks farewell to the Ephesian elders as the scene's observable response or movement.
observations.label: Paul speaks farewell to the Ephesian elders

observations.body: The passage places God beside Paul speaks farewell to the Ephesian elders.
observations.label: God

payload.posture: Read Acts 20:17–38 as one movement in Paul's story, keeping the passage's actions, setting, sequence, and limits visible.
payload.tension: The passage states paul speaks farewell to the Ephesian elders. From Miletus he sent to Ephesus and called to himself the elders of the assembly. sorrowing most of all because of the word which he had spoken, that they should see his face no more. Then they accompanied him to the ship. It does not by itself supply every cause or later interpretation of this part of Paul's story.
